capabilities: Assign codes to paragraphs via bidirectional wikilinks between data and code files
Create structured extraction files from templates using YAML frontmatter
Rename, merge, and delete codes and extractions while updating all references
Track analysis progress and theoretical saturation with counters and charts
extras: Recommends using a separate vault for analysis; modifies some Obsidian core behavior (deletion monitoring, block-reference styling); migration from other QDA software is not supported; free for academic use with a recommended APA citation; developer accepts GitHub Sponsors support.
intentEvidence: It is an open alternative to MAXQDA and atlas.ti, using Markdown to store data and codes.
motivation: The author, a sociologist doing PhD research, was inspired by a blog post by Ryan Murphy and wanted free, open, future-proof QDA tooling.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in qualitative data analysis workflow, and commercial QDA software like MAXQDA or atlas.ti is proprietary, licensed, and stores data in non-open formats.
